name: The Stair of Nine Cisterns
region_detail: A sandstone canyon within territory claimed by the Veyrathi.
site_type: waterworks | Ancient sites; abandoned infrastructure | Ancient high-elven hydraulic works and subterranean inspection chambers.
history: Ancient high-elven engineers constructed nine stone basins at successive elevations within the canyon, connecting them through underground conduits. The installation predates the present division between the Qasari and Veyrathi. Later generations maintained portions of the works, but knowledge of the deeper system gradually diminished.
current_state: Several upper basins have recently emptied despite retaining water in previous seasons. Veyrathi scouts have found fresh sediment and damaged masonry near an inspection opening. The relationship between these changes and the declining Qasari wells has not been established. The Veyrathi restrict access pending an assessment of the site.
inhabitants: Occasional Canyon Scout patrols and Veyrathi scholars; desert wildlife. Any occupants of the deeper chambers remain undetermined.
danger_level: Moderate due to steep approaches, unstable masonry, and uncertain water movements; potentially high in the deeper passages.
points_of_interest:
Nine stepped cisterns; ancient water-level markings; stone distribution channels; inspection shafts; partially exposed conduit; carved maintenance inscriptions; sealed lower chamber.

Unresolved elements: The original extent and operation of the hydraulic system; Whether the damage is natural, deliberate, or supernatural; Which conduits supply the modern Qasari wells; Whether the system can be investigated or repaired without disturbing protected ancestral sites.
discovery: A sandstone canyon within territory claimed by the Veyrathi. Veyrathi archives preserve records of the installation. Ilyen Seret and Kesira Vayn may identify the approach; Qasari water records may contain references to the older conduits.
related_records:
Faction Plot: P-009 — The Wells of the Ancients — Direct. The installation provides a potential means of investigating the disrupted ancient watercourse; the source of the disruption remains undetermined.

Notable individuals and factions: Sarith al-Vey (N-051) — concerned with protecting the ancestral installation; Kesira Vayn (N-052) — oversees patrols in the canyons and may facilitate a cooperative investigation; Ilyen Seret (N-053) — may interpret surviving technical records; Nahira sa-Qesh (N-048) — seeks restoration of affected Qasari water supplies.
